reasons: (a) On the trigger (compare(-0.0f, -1.2f), NumberUtilsTest.java:1132) keyOf returns the raw IEEE bit pattern, so negative values get keys in reverse order (key(-0.0f)=Integer.MIN_VALUE < key(-1.2f)); this violates keyOf's own contract 'Values are put in order by comparing their keys'. Hop 4 compares the two keys exactly as documented (lower key first, same key 0); hops 1-3 are documented as comparing 'by their sort keys' and delegate faithfully; the facade's wrong answer is pure propagation. The gold is the only method that violates its contract given correct callees. (b) Every hop's javadoc matches its code; the hop 1-3 phrase 'comes before' is tied to 'by their sort keys', and hop 4 fixes the comparison as signed 'lower key first', so no hop can be read as the owner without contradicting its own doc. (c) Four non-gold edits pass the trigger, the five ownership tests and the full suite (hop 1 relational short-circuit, hop 3 argument swap on two sign-negative values, hop 4 reversed comparison for two negative keys, facade subtraction per the lie), but each contradicts its own javadoc ('by their sort keys' / 'lower key comes first') or leaves the chain dead for non-tied inputs, and all leave keyOf's documented contract violated, so they are bypasses, not competing repairs. The spec's three declared compensating edits are one-sided and fail the trigger (G9). (d) Hop names (orderValues, orderByKey, keyOrder, compareKeys, keyOf) are neutral; no comments or fault vocabulary; the lie ('The difference of the two values is computed first, and the order is read from that difference before any other test is made.') describes subtraction and names neither keys, sign handling nor negatives. (e) Gold is exactly five calls below the facade; hops are in five distinct existing classes (ToStringStyle, StringUtils, ArrayUtils, FastDateFormat, StrBuilder); facade body is one delegating call (the original had no guard); one added procedural lie sentence not performed by the code; the gold javadoc is silent on the negative-key step; the trigger is an existing test and, on a clean recompile, is the only failing test of the full suite; correct.patch makes the trigger pass. (f) The ordering of negative floats by value is pinned outside the gold: deprecated org.apache.commons.lang.NumberUtils.compare(float,float) and its passing testCompareFloat (asserts compare(-0.0f,-1.2f)==+1, compare(-1.2f,-MAX)==+1), the double overload math.NumberUtils.compare(double,double) and its passing testCompareDouble (same assertions for doubles), and the facade's own largest-to-smallest ordering list.
